chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Said from Safwan ibn Yahya from Ibn Muskān from al-Ḥalabī said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about hunting: a man throws (a spear) and hits it obliquely, killing it, and he had named (God) when he threw it, but the iron (tip) did not hit it. He said: 'If the spear that hit it is the one that killed it, then if he sees it, let him eat it.'
ai.seo_question: Is hunted game halal if the spear kills it but the metal tip doesn't hit the body?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) clarifies the condition of *tadhkiyah* (naming God) for game killed by projectile force rather than direct impact, ruling that the prey is halal if the specific projectile used caused the death. This highlights the Shia juristic principle that the efficacy of the name depends on the causal agent of death, reinforcing the importance of intention and verbal invocation in hunting rituals. The ruling underscores the flexibility in Islamic dietary laws regarding the method of kill, provided the essential conditions of naming and permissible animals are met.
